Siri AI is a major upgrade for Apple's assistant, already available on iOS 27. I noticed a standout difference between it and other AI assistants, and it's a good one.

The all-new Siri on iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, unlike every other AI chatbot

Since the first beta of iOS 27 launched, I've been using Siri AI for almost four months. Overall, it meets all the expectations I had for it.

The all-new Siri is far more powerful than its predecessor, fulfilling the original promise of becoming a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

However, I have to admit: if you need the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tools, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be better suited for you.

That said, after using Siri AI and then comparing it with those third-party tools, I noticed a key difference that made me clearly lean toward Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It's not overly verbose, nor does it mimic human-like personalities that lead people to unconsciously form personal relationships with it.

Siri is helpful, smart, and agile, doing what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you that it's an AI, so it might make mistakes. It also won't pretend to date you.

In contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all full of personality and opinions, displaying more human-like qualities, which to me doesn't feel genuine enough.

I suppose some users enjoy this more 'personal' approach. But I'd much rather have AI assistants stick to their job and not pretend to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has built the all-new Siri accordingly.

What do you think about how 'human-like' AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
